data_points.source_name: bpc-intel derived (MOFSL income-cohort spend x in-band MRP)
data_points.methodology: AFFORDABILITY RATIO, [ESTIMATE] derived from two ledgered figures, not measured. Numerator: an in-band shelf price (MRP). Denominator: MOFSL/Company annual BPC spend per consumer for the highest income cohort (>USD15k p.a.), USD140, converted at the pinned USD/INR 96.23 (config/exchange_rates.yaml, 2026-07-21) = Rs13,472. BASIS MISMATCH stated deliberately: the denominator is annual outlay across ALL BPC categories and ALL channels (organised + unorganised), the numerator is one skincare SKU's MRP in the online channel, so the ratio overstates nothing about margin and is only an affordability index. SENSITIVITY: at Rs1,500 / Rs1,900 / Rs2,900 MRP the ratio is 11.1% / 14.1% / 21.5% against the USD140 cohort, and 13.4% / 17.0% / 26.0% against the mid-level-professional cohort (USD116 = Rs11,163). Purchase frequency for these cohorts is 17-18 occasions a year (MOFSL Exhibit 14), implying ~Rs748 average spend per occasion for the top cohort — an in-band SKU at Rs1,900 is ~2.5x that.
data_points.notes: [PREMIUM-SKIN] ONE in-band SKU at Rs1,900 MRP absorbs ~14.1% of the ENTIRE annual BPC budget of India's highest-income consumer cohort (>USD15k p.a., USD140/yr). Rs1,900 is the list price Phase 1 recommends as the floor for holding the band after discounting. Read as the trial constraint on this band: the purchase is a budget event, not a top-up.

data_points.source_name: EximGuru, Indian customs duty for tariff item 33049910 (face creams)
data_points.notes: [PREMIUM-SKIN] BASIC CUSTOMS DUTY on Indian tariff item 33049910, assessed on CIF value. STALE AND RECORDED AS SUCH: the page's most recent entry is dated 02-Feb-2018, when BCD was raised from 10% to 20%. NOT verified against a current CBIC notification, so it is a 2018 MFN reference rate, not a confirmed 2026 rate. Same page gives Social Welfare Surcharge 10% (levied on the BCD itself, so ~2% of CIF) and IGST 18%. IGST is CREDITABLE and is working capital, not margin — only BCD and SWS stick to a P&L. period recorded as 2018 rather than 2026 precisely so this is not read as current. The India-Korea CEPA may reduce this to zero for Korean-origin goods against a Form AK certificate of origin, but no page stating a preferential rate for HS 3304 could be fetched and verified, so Phase 4 models both 0% and 20% rather than assuming either.

data_points.source_name: EximGuru, Indian customs duty for tariff item 33049910 (face creams)
data_points.notes: [PREMIUM-SKIN] IGST at import on tariff item 33049910, which also implies the domestic GST rate on the good. CREDITABLE input tax — affects working capital, never margin, and Phase 4's model excludes it from the P&L and reports it separately. Same staleness caveat as the BCD row: the page's most recent entry is 02-Feb-2018, and this has NOT been re-verified against the September-2025 GST slab restructure. A slab move would change every revenue line in the Phase 4 model, because India's MRP is GST-inclusive and revenue is MRP/(1+GST). Flagged in the model's assumptions block as an unverified input.
